L0.contract: Course v1 S1-S6 with the wheeled annex. Apparatus smoke test: proves achievability by this rover; does not exclude controller, engine or fixture causes of a later failure.

L1a.contract: Course v1 standalone: initial stable hold, at least 8 strict alternating forward touchdowns, net displacement at least L, terminal stable hold for 5 seconds; complete within 60 seconds, all whole-run invariants apply.

L1b.contract: THE COURSE, segment S1 (Approach): walk from stable hold to the ramp entry. >=4 strict alternating touchdowns, cross-track <=0.15 m, path efficiency >=0.70, stance slip <=0.02 m.

L1c.contract: THE COURSE, segments S2+S3 (Descent, Advance): walk DOWN the ramp with no fall and no forbidden support, >=2 touchdowns on the ramp, stance slip <=0.06 m, arrive with both pads on the ground; then >=5 further strict alternating steps, each forward projection >0.02 m.

L1d.contract: Course v1 S1-S6 unbroken, legged annex, all frozen held-out robustness cases. Includes closed loop, ascent and return to the original plate pose; at most 240 seconds.

L2.contract: Two runs of the same inputs under TWO DIFFERENT recorded renamings produce an identical deterministicProjection(frame) after remapping references. Distinct from D1: D1 fixes the renaming seed and varies nothing, so it cannot catch identity dependence.

D1.contract: Same blueprint, input trace AND renaming seed => identical deterministicProjection(frame) hash, two processes, both clocks. The projection excludes wall-clock timings, identifier mappings and diagnostic metadata.

P1.contract: BOTH must hold on a named scene and machine, over a stated measurement duration: >=30 rendered fps AND 120 completed simulation ticks per wall-clock second, with a declared overload policy. A responsive renderer over a simulation accruing debt is not a pass. Measure before setting any budget.

S1.contract: A hostile controller cannot escape, hang, or read undeclared state.

F1.contract: F1 v2: the maintainer-designated target player accepts the basic construction experience after building something that moves within 15 minutes without live assistance, and wants to build another. Returning sessions are eligible; explicit real-player feedback and the served build are required. The latest assessment governs.

F2.contract: Instrumented: application response time across one place -> connect -> run cycle on a named reference scene and machine (input event to reflecting frame, plus Run to first tick), human thinking time excluded. p95 under 2 s, no single stall over 500 ms.

F3.contract: A player who did not build the machine can say why it failed from the post-mortem alone.

F4.contract: Ten minutes of unassisted play yields one moment of visible delight and no moment of 'I don't know what this wants from me'.

F5.contract: A player, using their own browser agent, gets an actionable answer to 'why isn't this working' without leaving the game. Judged by watching a person.

rules.rule: Layer imports follow the module graph and physical laws receive no identity.
Nine ordered phases, one integration, previous completed sensors.
Physical properties derive only from authored geometry and player selections.
Checks execute, deadlines interrupt, owners and references validate.
The local CI command finishes in less than 180 seconds.
Runtime v1 governs values, cursor epochs, bounded replay and current save-format admission.
All five measured physical stages must pass before expanding terrain.
Course v1 and its annexes require frozen fixtures and unbroken qualification.
Players and their agents share one command surface and physical constraints.

checks.description: module graph: layer ownership and allowed import edges
specific invariant positive and negative control suites from manifest pointers
checked production boundary interfaces, schema-derived freshness and wrong-type counterexamples

M0.how: CI runs the every-commit tier in under 3 minutes
every check and obligation names a ruleId or barId it enforces; unowned entries are rejected; rules[] is non-empty
Evidence and runner counterexamples pass under node:test.

M1.how: a bundle replays to the same failure
the physics-library choice is recorded as an ADR with its reasoning; stepping, determinism and checkpoints all depend on it, so it cannot wait for M2

M2.how: every malformed fixture is rejected with a specific error
exactly one module imports the physics library
no live library object is reachable from any export (G2)
parts and UI features carry a milestone field and the build rejects anything above the current milestone

M3.how: controllers demonstrably cannot read live state

renaming every part/component/blueprint/role id leaves the deterministic projection unchanged, on the scenarios that exist at M3 -- built BEFORE there is a contact law to corrupt (L2 at M8 expands the scenario set, it does not introduce the check)

M3b.how: default keyboard control runs through the ordinary command bus and Command Receivers; M3's host-side test double does not ship

M4b.how: per-pad normal force, sole clearance, touchdown/unload events, COM and support-polygon margin are measured -- a probe that cannot measure clearance cannot demonstrate it
demonstrated after any repair, probe rerun
demonstrated after any repair, probe rerun
demonstrated after any repair, probe rerun
demonstrated after any repair, probe rerun
demonstrated after any repair, probe rerun

M5.how: plate height, ramp slope, approach distance, L, circle bound, ramp-foot capture radius and return tolerance are recorded and fingerprinted BEFORE the L0 attempt and not changed to accommodate the machine
the six-segment evaluator, machine bindings, measurement frames and position-based state machine exist and run -- L0 is an M5 gate and cannot be met by an M6 evaluator
Measure torque, current and energy demand against physical ratings at the frozen slope. Diagnose failures with clearance, contact, control and engine hypotheses as well as power.
rover drives over uneven ground repeatably; distance/repeats set from first measurement
rated capacity per joint, transmitted-load computation and a break event exist; a phase that computes nothing does not satisfy 'no damage'
no §3 circuit predicate names a gait; gait-specific predicates live in the legged/wheeled annexes. An evaluator keyed on machine type is the same defect class as a friction law keyed on rigRole.

every Course predicate has BOTH a trace it accepts and a deliberately-wrong trace it rejects -- an evaluator nobody has seen reject anything is not known to work (the same rule as 'never trust a test you have not seen fail', applied to the evaluator)

M6.how: an induced stall produces a bundle that replays to the same failure on a named lane
the legged annex predicates (touchdowns, alternation, stance slip) and support-eligibility validation for legged fixtures

M8b.how: F1 still passes with the WebMCP tools unregistered -- the agent is an accelerator, never a crutch
no tool name or description interpolates player-authored content (part names, blueprint titles, error strings)
the tool set is registered once; no third-party script can add or modify tools (mid-session tool injection)
no tool exposes a capability the player's own UI does not -- the agent is a player
tool results carry closed-enum reason codes; player-authored strings appear only in delimited data fields

positive.anchor: disconnect undo redo preserve authored history and reject bad edits atomically
mixed resize, axle attachment, rotation, undo and reload preserve connections

negative.anchor: malformed authoring is rejected without altering model or cursor
registered edit examples share rejection and round-trip behavioral contracts

placement commits valid previews once, rejects stale completions and cancels pointer ownership

invariants.guarantee: Authored wheel geometry drives physical radius and mass; attachment admission rejects real intersections while allowing empty hull corners.

positive.anchor: wheel diameter changes physical radius and mass without moving its axle; undo and load preserve it

negative.anchor: wheel bounds corners are empty while real cylinder intersections are blocked

invariants.guarantee: Names and rig placement do not select physical materials; authored selectable materials are copied.

positive.anchor: authored selectable material is copied without identity inference

negative.anchor: renaming and rig placement never select material mass or contact properties

invariants.guarantee: Valid checkpoint restore preserves future physical stepping while invalid restore remains atomic.

positive.anchor: checkpoint restores tick and future physics but advances observation epoch

negative.anchor: checkpoint rejection is atomic for malformed clocks inputs sensors and identity

invariants.guarantee: Existing mirror copies allocate fresh identities, preserve authored fields and internal connections, and remain independent through editing and persistence.

positive.anchor: public mirror transactions isolate instance parameter edits and preserve both graphs through Undo and save/load

negative.anchor: copied graph oracle rejects lost authored fields, topology corruption, aliases and external leakage

invariants.guarantee: Connection display preserves authored edges and uses exact diagnostic path IDs; hidden render resources do not intercept picking.

positive.anchor: render producer uses exact test edges and preserves source and endpoint poses

negative.anchor: hidden render resources neither intercept rays nor churn geometry and restore current endpoints
